### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via execCtx (symbol, a field of type RecycleBinSystemInsertOrganization))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `438400c6eb08540baececda1b31c3c120e063d7e` — the merge of head `4bd70f0a1c2f24f3dbad9f41e65ccd01e883c513` into base `493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 438400c6eb08540baececda1b31c3c120e063d7e && git checkout 438400c6eb08540baececda1b31c3c120e063d7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 4bd70f0a1c2f24f3dbad9f41e65ccd01e883c513 && git checkout -B drift-repro 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3 && git merge --no-ff 4bd70f0a1c2f24f3dbad9f41e65ccd01e883c513

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 493ad095d40ece94fe25d822566138fd01f5d4c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36097 · head `4bd70f0a1c` · **ACCEPT** (CI not concluded; one owed sentence) · 2026-11-21T13:26Z

Card #35667. I read the claim 7061800429, the route-B amendment 7062354282, both reports (7062012198, 7063245386) and the full diff against `7ba22bb6ee` (5 files, +241/−7). The PR declares Clause-② no and Metadata-protocol none, and touches no spec or governed path.

### What holds
- **One resolver, no second spelling.** `bin.write()` now takes the engine's own `MiddlewareAndContextFacet.resolveSystemInsertOrganization`, reached through `middlewareAndContextHost.of(this.facade)`. That is the same body the engine's insert calls, and `engine.ts` stays at 6857 lines. `write()` asks it only when neither the record's tenant column nor the context names an organization. Read against `engine-middleware-and-context.ts:348`, the resolver behaves as follows:
  - **When it answers `undefined`:** if the context carries a `tenantId`, or the object is federated, has no tenant field, or every row is already stamped.
  - **Single posture:** answers the derived Default Organization.
  - **No organization object registered:** answers `undefined`, which is D9's lean-embedding note.
  - **Otherwise:** throws `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError`.
- **Fails before anything is removed.** `write()` runs after the cascade walk and before `driver.delete`, so a refusal leaves the root row in place, and the pins show no entry stays. Permanent and `multi` deletes open no capture (`openRecycleBinCapture(…, multi || permanent)`), so they are untouched.
- **Pins assert code and status, on both legs.**
  - **sqlite** (`packages/runtime`):
    - `single`: the entry carries `DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID` and a restore brings the record back.
    - CONTROL: a context naming `org_named` still owns the entry.
    - `isolated`: refused with `{ code: 'ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED', status: 500 }`, the record still there and no entry.
  - **The capture harness** (no NOT NULL) covers the same `single` and wall cases.
  - **Ablation:** 2 red per leg.
- **Memory-leg deviation accepted.** A new test consumer of `@objectstack/driver-memory` is a ruled disposition under `check:driver-memory-census`, and the harness keeps rows the way that driver does.
- **Fixture change accepted.** Seeding the Default Organization in the capture harness is what D9 requires once the resolver is in the path: a registered `sys_organization` with no rows is the "no derivable owner" refusal. The org-delete cascade test's opt-out is scoped to that test.
- **Changeset.** I checked it sentence by sentence and every sentence matches the code and pins.

### Owed (not a REWORK, but say it on the PR)
**O1. Why Clause-② is "no" when one store narrows.** The changeset says a memory-store delete "succeeded" before. Under a walled posture it is now refused, so on that store an operation that was accepted is now refused, which is the shape of `(narrowing)` under AGENTS.md rule 3. I read it as a bug fix, not a narrowing:
- every SQL store already failed that delete, on the bin's NOT NULL;
- memory accepted it only by writing a bin row that broke the bin's own invariant: an entry no organization owns, which no organization's listing or cascade reaches.

That reading is the seat's to state, not mine to assume. Add one `Clause-② basis:` line to the PR body, or declare `(narrowing)`, which brings CRT L2 and the breaking-change kit.

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1.** The new branch does not check `isSystem`: it runs for any delete whose record and context both name no organization. The changeset frames it as "a delete made under `{ isSystem: true }`". User contexts normally carry `tenantId`, so in practice this is the system door, but "a delete whose context names no organization (the system door, typically)" would be exact.
- **N2.** Under a wall, the changeset's remedy names `{ isSystem: true, tenantId }`. A `permanent: true` delete is the other route: it opens no bin, so the refusal does not apply. One clause would help an operator who wants the record gone, not binned.

### Owed
- **CI at `4bd70f0a1c`:** 11 success, 16 skipped and 13 in progress at this stamp, with no failure yet. That includes Test Core, the shards that would catch any existing test elsewhere that system-deletes an organization-less record under a wall on a store without NOT NULL. This ACCEPT holds on this head once CI is green.
- **O1 above.**
